title: Free Access to PersonaFi Beta Software Testing (Spending Forecast & Budget App via CSV Transaction List Upload) @ PersonaFi
body:
Deal: Free Access to PersonaFi Beta Software Testing (Spending Forecast & Budget App via CSV Transaction List Upload) @ PersonaFi

[kaiden] “ Upload a CSV export from your bank (CommBank, ANZ, etc.)”
This makes me wonder where this data is being stored and how that goes when it comes to data breach etc.
I’d rather something self hosted in an air gap to prevent others from seeing/sharing.
[tenpercent] Yeah. This would be a great ruse for organised crime to identify future victims.
[personafi] Fair question, and you're right to ask it of anything that wants your bank data.
Where it's stored: Google Cloud in Sydney. It's encrypted in transit and at rest, and there's no advertising or analytics tracking. I don't sell or share data with anyone.
What's kept: the transactions from your CSV, not the file itself. No bank logins or passwords ever. Sign-in is handled by Google, so I never see your PersonaFi password either.
The AI coach: it gets only the figures needed to answer your question, never your full transaction history. Names, account numbers, BSBs, emails and phone numbers are stripped before anything is sent. For CSV uploads that goes to OpenAI, with every request asking them not to store it, and they don't train on it. Chats are deleted after 90 days.
Your control: you can download everything or delete your account from Settings at any time, and deleting it wipes every record.
All that said, any cloud service carries some breach risk, and I won't pretend otherwise. If air-gapped and self-hosted is your bar, PersonaFi isn't that, and a local spreadsheet or self-hosted tool is the right call for you. Full details are in the privacy policy and security page on personafi.com.au.
[tenpercent] Can you see the data?
And if you say "no", why should we trust that response?
[personafi] Honest answer: yes, technically. I run the system, so I have access to the database, the same as the owner of any app you use. I don’t browse people’s transactions. I only look at an individual’s data if they ask me to fix something.
As for why you should trust that: you shouldn’t, on my word alone, and that’s a fair stance. What I can offer is what’s written in the privacy policy, that you can delete everything yourself at any time, and that nothing is sold or shared.
If you’d rather not upload anything, there’s a sample household at personafi.com.au/demo you can poke around in with made-up data. That way you can see whether it’s even useful before deciding.

[personafi] Good questions.
Do the first 50 sign ups get free lifetime access?
No pricing has been decided yet. When it goes paid, everyone who tests it during the beta gets 50% off for as long as they stay subscribed , as a thank you for putting up with the bugs.
What are the underlying assumptions? Can inflation and earning rates be adjusted?
12-month forecast: built from your own history. Regular bills repeat on their actual schedule, and everything else uses your 6-month average. You can override any line, e.g. "electricity is $180 a month from March".
Net worth plan: 3% income growth and 2.5% inflation by default, and both can be changed.
Each asset has its own growth rate , which you set: super, shares, property, savings interest.
Also editable: tax rate (30% default), retirement age (60) and Age Pension rules. You can view it in today's dollars or future dollars.
Does he take into account promo codes and discounted gift cards?
It works from what actually leaves your account. Buy a $100 gift card for $90 and it records $90 of spending, so the discount is already counted. Whatever you then buy with the card won't show up separately, though. Uncle Stavros would still ask why you needed the gift card in the first place.
